docs.purpose: Starts the subscribe flow for a signed-in user: checks they are not already subscribed, mid-cancellation or pending account deletion, then issues a short-lived single-use link to the checkout page so the URL is safe to share or log without exposing who the user is.
docs.data_story: It reads 2 tables — `user_profiles` and `entitlements` and writes `subscribe_nonces`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `mobile/src/hooks/useSubscribeCheckout.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Uses FOR UPDATE row locks on both user_profiles and the (uid,'lead_gen') entitlements row inside one transaction to close a TOCTOU race against a concurrent webhook. Reuses an existing unexpired nonce rather than always inserting a new one (idempotent within the 15-minute window). Distinct 400 codes route already-entitled, past_due (to the portal) and deletion-pending users differently instead of a generic error. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: No Stripe call at all — this route only mints the nonce; the Stripe Checkout Session is created downstream by /api/subscribe/exchange. resolveCheckoutBaseUrl() (:37-48) THROWS in non-production when SUBSCRIBE_CHECKOUT_BASE_URL is unset; that throw is raised at :80 inside the try and lands on the generic 500 at :237. CENSUS AGREEMENT: matches (reads user_profiles + entitlements; writes subscribe_nonces) — plus an unlisted READ of subscribe_nonces at :146, which the census's read list omits. | Idempotency: Guarded and safe to repeat within the nonce window: a still-unexpired nonce for the same user is SELECTed FOR UPDATE and reused instead of inserting a new row (:146-156), so a double-tapped CTA returns the same URL and does not pollute the table. The FOR UPDATE at :151 serialises concurrent same-user calls. The INSERT (:164) is backstopped by the `nonce` PRIMARY KEY (migrations/114:88). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control header, no revalidate/dynamic export (full file read :1-241) | Entitlement posture: getEntitlementStatusForUpdate(client, uid, DEFAULT_PRODUCT) at src/app/api/subscribe/session/route.ts:119 -> `SELECT status, trial_started_at FROM entitlements WHERE user_id = $1 AND product = $2 FOR UPDATE` (src/lib/entitlements/index.ts:116). Three gates on the result: DELETION_BLOCKED_STATUSES {'cancelled_pending_deletion'} :68/:121-126; PORTAL_ROUTED_STATUSES {'past_due'} :61/:127-129; ALREADY_ENTITLED_STATUSES {'active','admin_managed'} :53/:130-132. Plus an account-level `account_deleted_at` gate on the row-locked user_profiles read at :102-118. | Other guards / classification: Nonce MINTING side of the single-use contract: an unexpired nonce is reused under FOR UPDATE (:146-156) rather than churning new rows; otherwise a fresh randomUUID() is inserted (:158,:164-167). No signature/replay guard (this route is session-authenticated). | Locking tests: src/tests/subscribe-portal-session.infra.test.ts, src/tests/subscribe-session.infra.test.ts, src/tests/subscribe-session.security.test.ts.
